rules.name: A REAL FLAIR FOR DISCORD
rules.turn:
use-power S Pw, spirit:special S flair-for-discord, (add-strife V), at V L
  ^strife-added-by S Pw L
fast-phase, (strife-added-by S Pw L), >use-power S Pw
  ~flair S L
#acc flair-option : e
flair S L, at V L2, within-1 L L2, piece:kind V K, invader K / flair-option V
flair S L / flair-option decline
flair S L, energy S E, ge E 1
  ?[rng] V
  !(flair-option V)
  ~flair-choice S V
flair-choice S C, is C V, piece:kind V K, invader K
  ~>pay-energy S 1
  ~add-piece V strife
rules.evidence: seed 7: declines (energy stays 2); seeds 1-3: pay-energy trickster 1, extra Strife on an Invader in l1 or l2 (within 1 of l1); energy 1
rules.notes: Needed BASE-EXT Energy (@sum of signed changes), Strife, Range 1. The extra Strife must not re-trigger the rule: it is added with the physical `add-piece V strife` instead of the game verb `add-strife`, the same trick as Heavy Mining. That means other 'when Strife is added' rules (e.g. a future Senseless Roaming) would not see it either. Port to fresh-left ^ / #acc (2026-10-12): the generic `^phase` window no longer overlaps the phase's use-power episodes (each `^phase` starts at its own moment), so the trigger is anchored on the Fast and Slow phase episodes themselves (one rule each; the snippet shows the Fast one), peeking the trigger fact and continuing after the Power with `>use-power`. Options offered are unchanged; with seed 7 the rng now picks differently (an invader for the flair instead of decline, t2 instead of t1 to destroy), because option order follows store discovery order.
rules.text: After one of your Powers adds [Strife] in a land, you may pay 1 Energy to add 1 [Strife] within 1 [Range] of that land.

rules.name: CLEANING UP MESSES IS A DRAG
rules.turn:
use-power S Pw, spirit:special S cleaning-up-messes, neq Pw lets-see-what-happens,
  (remove-blight L)
  ^blight-removed-by S Pw
fast-phase, (blight-removed-by S Pw), >use-power S Pw
  ?[rng] P
  !(presence-of S P, at P L, land L)
  ~cleanup-destroy S P
cleanup-destroy S C, is C P, ~destroy-presence-of P
destroy-presence-of P, ~move P destroyed
rules.evidence: cleanse removes Blight -> cleanup-destroy, t1 destroyed; Let's See What Happens also removes Blight but no cleanup fires
rules.notes: 'Ignore this rule for Let's See What Happens' is a filter on the Power (`neq Pw lets-see-what-happens`), needing the user-defined neq js relation. Port to fresh-left ^ / #acc (2026-10-12): the generic `^phase` window no longer overlaps the phase's use-power episodes (each `^phase` starts at its own moment), so the trigger is anchored on the Fast and Slow phase episodes themselves (one rule each; the snippet shows the Fast one), peeking the trigger fact and continuing after the Power with `>use-power`. Options offered are unchanged; with seed 7 the rng now picks differently (an invader for the flair instead of decline, t2 instead of t1 to destroy), because option order follows store discovery order.
rules.text: After one of your Powers Removes [Blight] , Destroy 1 of your [Presence] . Ignore this rule for Let's See What Happens.

base_ext: Energy as @sum of signed changes (gain/pay); Strife as a piece located on an Invader; remove-blight (to the Blight Card) with a choice; within-1 (Range 1); per-phase triggers anchored on the Fast/Slow phase episodes (the generic `^phase` window no longer works under fresh-left ^). The played cards are a turn-scoped acc view (`#acc played`, `turn / played …`).
language_issues: Distinguishing 'added by a Power' from 'added by this special rule' needs two verbs for the same physical act; a rule-provenance notion would be cleaner.
No symbol inequality builtin; `neq` via #js-def JSON comparison.
Energy can't go below zero only by convention: nothing stops a payment exceeding the total except a guard in each paying rule (`energy S E, ge E 1`).
